text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] The Euphrates had flowed for ten thousand years. Then, in one summer, it stopped. First, the boats sat on the mud. Then the fish came up gasping, by the thousands. The wells went dry. Whole villages loaded their lives onto trucks. A can of water cost more than a day's work. And the great river shrank to a thin brown thread. And the old men began to remember. Fourteen centuries ago, the Prophet said this river would one day uncover a mountain of gold. And he left one warning: whoever is there should take nothing from it. Most people laughed. Then a girl chasing her goat across the riverbed saw something shine. She dug with her hands. It didn't end. Her father dug. Then the whole village dug. It wasn't a coin. It wasn't a nugget. It went down further than anyone could see. By nightfall, the news had crossed every border. By morning, a million people were walking toward the river.
